## Gates

`just check` runs `ops-check`, `ops-docs check`, `tasks check`, assembly validation
and Python compilation. `python3 bin/assemble-instructions check` compares the
selected artifact and manifest with the catalog and the live ops renderer.
Relevant staged changes select the entire index; otherwise it checks disk.
The executing assembler must equal its index bytes in a staged check.

Use `just test-one tools/test_assemble_instructions.py -k staged` for staged cases.
`just test-fast` and `just test` both run all tests in `tools/`; there is no
affected-only selection. The pre-push hook carries the full suite; there is no CI.
Historical proof commands are acceptance checks outside the recurring gates.

## Layout

- `instructions/AGENTS.md`: generated global instructions served through hq
  `./links.toml`; `instructions/AGENTS.manifest.json`: generated provenance.
  Root `AGENTS.md` is this repository's guide.
- `instructions/assembly.toml` and `instructions/fragments/`: editable catalog and
  policy sources. Ops owns the external Projects fragment.
- `profiles/`: the personal, work and external fragments resolved by ops-profile.
- `skills/`: seven vendored skills, the `curate-docs` skill, `skills/references/` and
  the skill README.
- `vendor/superpowers`: the pinned submodule; `just setup` initializes it.
- `.skill-lock.json`: skill source metadata. `bin/skill-sizes.py`: the inventory utility.
- `docs/notes/`, `docs/specs/`, `docs/plans/`: the briefs, designs and plans the code
  cites; the rest live in the records root (`tasks where` names it). `docs/`: coding advice and the provenance audit.
  `docs/archive/`: old instruction text awaiting review; its README lists it.
- `hooks/claude-profile`: the SessionStart hook every Claude Code and Codex session runs,
  wired from hq's hook files; it reaches ops's resolver through the tasks registry.
- `bin/assemble-instructions`: the sole artifact/manifest writer and guard.
  `tools/`: assembly tests, pinned proof driver and vendored tooling;
  task records live in the records root.

## Rules

- `hooks/claude-profile` never exits non-zero and never blocks a session; every failure is
  one `profile: unresolved` line. A change to it is verified by the text a fresh session
  shows, never by its exit status, which proves nothing.

- The linked global artifact and manifest are generated; do not edit either by
  hand. Edit `instructions/fragments/…`, then run `just assemble`.
- The manifest records `bin/assemble-instructions`' own blob id and sha256, so an
  edit to the assembler stales it even when the rendered instructions are unchanged.
  Run `just assemble` and stage the manifest in the same commit; only its assembler
  entry may change.
- Ops owns the Projects/Feedback-owners source. Edit identity declarations there,
  run just projects in ops, then `just assemble` here. Assembly is the only writer
  of delivered instructions and provenance; both checks must pass.
- Deployed gates always use registered owner roots. Preparation environment
  values cannot redirect them; explicit CLI source overrides announce their
  input and require the registered repository identity.
- Keep `vendor/superpowers` at the release Claude Code's installed plugin runs
  (`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`). A bump that adds or removes a skill
  needs a commit here and a declaration in hq `./links.toml`, or harnesses run
  different skills.
